subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-profile managed-browser proxy config plus per-agent/subagent default browser-profile binding, and what security model should govern proxy credentials, SSRF enforcement, profile selection, and concurrent browser resource limits?
rationale: The request adds public config/API surface and changes browser egress plus cookie/session isolation semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security boundary from source inspection alone.

options.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
options.body: Add the feature only with a documented contract for SecretRef-safe proxy auth, explicit SSRF proxy trust, profile inheritance and override rules, diagnostics, and resource limits.

options.title: Keep explicit workarounds
options.body: Decline first-class per-agent/per-profile config for now and document explicit `profile`, `browser.extraArgs`, remote CDP, node-host, and external browser-lock patterns as the supported path.

options.title: Split into narrower canonicals
options.body: Move proxy egress decisions to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/60035 and browser ownership/inheritance decisions to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/85672, then retire this umbrella only after that maintainer split is explicit.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
recommendation.body: Add the feature only with a documented contract for SecretRef-safe proxy auth, explicit SSRF proxy trust, profile inheritance and override rules, diagnostics, and resource limits.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent browser plugin/config/docs ownership makes this the best available routing target for the product and security-boundary decision.
